_doc: Monotone-shrink ratchet budget for the conformance matrix. Each key is the exact suite name emitted by conformance-matrix.py; `ledgered` is the allowed count of ledgered gaps (the XFail/Skip column). The gate asserts the live count EQUALS this budget: a larger count (a regressed or newly-ledgered gap) fails RED, and a smaller count (a fixed gap) also fails RED until the budget is lowered here to lock the gain. This budget is authoritative and may only ever be edited DOWNWARD; a raise must be justified in review. Reasons describe the technical gap only.

SPARQL 1.1/1.2 evaluation (full corpus).note: 5 upstream-errata fixtures with non-canonical XSD lexicals (cast-decimal/double/float, coalesce01, plus-1-corrected); the entailment-regime cases (OWL-Direct/DL via the SHOIQ(D) tableau, RIF-rule, RDF-axiomatic-triple) are all native now

SPARQL CONSTRUCT (first-party corpus).note: no ledgered gaps: every case in crates/sparql-conformance/corpus/construct/ is graded, and a first-party corpus that ledgers its own cases would be grading itself against whatever the engine happens to do. The corpus carries both CONSTRUCT forms case for case - the SPARQL 1.1 16.2 triple-producing form, whose expected results are Turtle so a statement that gained a graph term would no longer match, and the quad-producing CONSTRUCT GRAPH <iri> form, whose expected results are N-Quads carrying a graph the template names on every line. Every one of the 10 triple-form evaluation cases has a graph-prefixed quad-form counterpart, and the corpus test checks that pairing rather than asserting it: the rewrite, the CONSTRUCT WHERE short form, the unbound-variable skip, the literal-subject skip, the triple-term-subject skip, the NESTED triple-term-subject skip, per-row blank freshness, a GRAPH-scoped WHERE, the solution modifiers, and an RDF 1.2 reifier + annotation template. The 16.2 subject rule is graded on BOTH kinds of term a subject position refuses, because RDF 1.2 data puts a triple term in reach of an ordinary triple pattern and an engine that recognised only the literal half would hard-fail on annotated input rather than skip one statement; and at BOTH depths the rule applies, because RDF 1.2 nests a triple term only in the OBJECT of another triple term. The nested depth is graded separately because it fails differently: an ill-formed asserted subject is refused downstream whatever the template rule says, while an ill-formed nested one is not - an engine enforcing the term model only at the asserted level emits the statement at exit status zero, into a document its own N-Triples/N-Quads/Turtle readers then refuse to parse, and persists it on an UPDATE path. Nine quad-form cases have no triple-form twin by nature - graphReifierScope pins the RDF 1.2 statement layer's per-graph keying (one reifier id, one annotation predicate, two graphs; an annotation in the graph that declares the reifier and an ordinary quad in the graph that does not), which needs two graphs to say anything, and the eight syntax verdicts grade the quad-template grammar itself. Those eight bound it from BOTH sides: one positive spelling that parses, and seven refused spellings established empirically against the parser rather than assumed - a missing graph name, a literal graph name and a blank-node graph name (the name is a VarOrIri), a nested GRAPH block and a GRAPH block missing its braces (a block body is a TriplesTemplate), a GRAPH block in the CONSTRUCT short form (whose one block is read twice, as template and as WHERE algebra), and a property path inside a GRAPH block (a template asserts triples, inside a block exactly as outside one). A corpus that pinned only what is accepted would let the grammar widen unnoticed

SPARQL DESCRIBE (first-party corpus).note: no ledgered gaps. SPARQL 1.1 16.4 leaves the description implementation-defined, so no vendored W3C manifest grades a DESCRIBE and this row is the form's only conformance measurement: it pins the engine's documented Symmetric Concise Bounded Description clause by clause - outgoing edges, incoming edges, the blank-node closure, the RDF 1.2 statement layer (the reifiers whose reified triple's subject OR object lies in the closure, together with their annotations - both sides of that disjunction measured separately, the object side isolated on a term that is the subject of nothing and whose reified triple is unasserted, and clause 3 composed with clause 4 through a blank reifier and a blank annotation object), the three target-resolution rules (concrete IRI, bound variable, *), the fact that a non-IRI binding describes nothing, and that a described statement stays in the graph it came from at every layer - the base quad, the reifier declaration and the annotation alike. That last claim is carried by three cases read over TriG and expected as N-Quads, so every expected row pins a graph; the other clause-4 cases read a default-graph-only fixture whose graph-less expectations cannot observe where a described statement lands, only that it was selected. Those three fix the extractor's selection/emission split: a reifier declaration is selected by its reified triple's subject-or-object membership in the closure and by nothing else - graph membership takes no part in the selection - and is re-emitted into the graph that declared it, so a declaration made in one graph about a triple asserted in another is kept where it was declared; and an annotation rides with the declaration it annotates rather than with the reifier resource, which one reifier id declared in two graphs, annotated in each under the same predicate, measures

SPARQL CDT (SEP-0009, vendored corpus).note: no ledgered gaps: all 658 cases the pinned upstream commit (awslabs/SPARQL-CDTs e0a746561ad6a2db0f70fdcccb57eadea04f50c8) declares are run and pass. Six groups - the cdt:List and cdt:Map function libraries, the FOLD aggregate, the UNFOLD graph pattern, ORDER BY over composite values, and blank-node identity inside composite lexical forms. This row is an INDEPENDENT oracle: until it existed every claim about this engine's CDT behavior rested on tests written beside the implementation by the same hand, which grade the engine against itself. Read together with one divergence that no number in this row can express: PurRDF's reader accepts two element forms the published SEP-0009 lexical space does not - an RDF 1.2 triple term and a directional language-tagged literal - because refusing an RDF 1.2 term type is not an admissible outcome for this toolkit, and a form outside the spec's lexical space is emitted only for a value the spec cannot express at all. A conformant SEP-0009 reader handed one of those literals WILL call it ill-formed. The mitigation is executed, not argued: crates/sparql-conformance/tests/cdt_lexical_divergence.rs tokenizes every corpus file this workspace ships with the production lexers, recovers every cdt:List/cdt:Map literal, and grades each one - all of them land inside the published space, so no vector anywhere here can tell PurRDF's reader from a strict one. Its counts are pinned as equalities, including the count of files the lexer refuses (13, every one a negative-syntax vector), each of which is text-checked for the SEP-0009 namespace rather than skipped. Note what that does and does not establish: the mitigation was originally specified over upstream NEGATIVE-SYNTAX entries, and as stated it is vacuous, because all 658 upstream entries are mf:QueryEvaluationTest and upstream ships no negative-syntax CDT vector at all. The broader claim the scan does establish is the one that matters, and it is re-checked on every re-vendor

SPARQL execution governors.note: no ledgered gaps: every case in vectors/sparql-governors/ is graded, and there is nothing a governor case could be excused for. The corpus carries a zero, a boundary (the ceiling IS the measured cost or complete stop-poll count, and must be admitted) and an over-bound (one below that measurement, and must trip) case for each of the five caller-settable numeric dimensions and for a deterministic injected deadline signal, plus the RDF 1.2 statement layer, the federated SERVICE transport seam, and the property-function relation seam. The property-function pair is banded three more times to take the two charge points apart — an invocation-isolating lane whose relation emits nothing, a row-isolating lane driven by a single row, and a 1200-row lane above the evaluator's fork threshold whose boundary is the sequential/parallel parity claim — and a seam case pins a fuel ceiling landing between an invocation and its first row. A separate wall-deadline smoke case pins only what a time-dependent trip can guarantee

SPARQL embedding kNN (first-party).note: no ledgered gaps: 11 first-party cases grading the PURREMB kNN property-function seam from query text through the shipped stack, and there is nothing a case here could be excused for. This row counts TEST FUNCTIONS, not fixtures - the lane has no corpus, because its subject is a seam rather than a document format, and its fixtures are PURREMB artifacts sealed in-process by purrdf_core's own writer. 10 of the 11 are the e2e surface: rank order, an unregistered IRI reading as an ordinary triple pattern, join-back by basic graph pattern, the LIMIT-is-a-prefix law at every k, byte identity across two independently built artifacts, the true k-nearest of a crowded space, and four governor cases pinning that the search is charged in proportion to the candidates EXAMINED rather than the rows returned - which is the property-function-work charge point the governor corpus cannot band, every relation in that corpus being a scripted fixture that reports zero work. The 11th is the cross-target pin: five neighbours and their exact xsd:double distance lexicals held as a Rust literal rather than recomputed, because a test that recomputes its expectation with the kernel under test agrees with any kernel at all. Its wasm32 half runs under make wasm-test, so this row measures the native target only, and the knn unit tests in the crate's lib are graded by make check rather than here

GeoSPARQL 1.1 (first-party).note: no ledgered gaps: 33 first-party cases across the two evaluator seams, the shape surface and the determinism pin. This row counts TEST FUNCTIONS, not fixtures. It is also the one row in this matrix with NO independent oracle behind it, and that is a real limit rather than a formality: no OGC GeoSPARQL 1.1 conformance suite is vendored here and none is claimed. The 12 SHACL cases are first-party shapes written in example.org space that structurally mirror the shipped OGC 22-047r1 validator shape for shape, because vendoring the validator verbatim would smuggle a real ontology's IRIs into a fixture and assert a default namespace this toolkit does not have - PurRDF mints no vocabulary IRIs. So these 33 grade the implementation against its own reading of the specification, and a misreading of OGC 22-047r1 would pass. What they do grade independently of that reading is EXACTNESS: 9 query-rewrite cases cover all four geo: relation branches and their join-back, 5 scalar-function cases cover the geof: accessors, measures and constructors plus the twelve registered-but-unimplemented functions that must abort the query BY NAME rather than answer a default, and 3 determinism cases fold a pinned u64 digest over the serialized bytes - WKT and GeoJSON renderings, DE-9IM matrix strings, exact decimal measures and IEEE bit patterns - of a 20-geometry corpus. That digest's cross-target half, native = wasm32 = the pinned golden, is a separate gate (make geo-determinism) because it needs the wasm32 target and Node; the crate's lib unit tests are graded by make check rather than here

Entailment (OWL 2 DL consistency).note: vendored W3C OWL 2 suite (262 consistency/inconsistency cases) graded against the OWL-Direct SHOIQ(D) tableau; 4 ledgered divergences, each typed in crates/sparql-conformance/src/owl2.rs::LEDGER — 2 bottom-property (the empty built-in role reads as an ordinary named role; the run RAISES the builtin-role boundary for it), 1 empty-domain (OWL 2 forbids the empty interpretation domain) and 1 withheld run (a cyclic class expression the parser refuses). Lowered from 5: the datatype-range decider gives the tableau a concrete domain, so a functional data property with two different literal values now clashes instead of merging the two literal nodes, and new-feature-keys-006 agrees with its published verdict. Lowered from 28 before that: the reverse mapping now reads the role characteristics (transitive/symmetric/asymmetric/reflexive/irreflexive/inverse-functional), role and property disjointness, owl:differentFrom and owl:AllDifferent, owl:AllDisjointClasses, owl:hasKey, owl:hasSelf and owl:NegativePropertyAssertion instead of dropping them, and the sameAs re-statement pass no longer tries to put a literal in subject position. No ledgered divergence is an unsoundness. Consistency-shaped: this row does NOT measure the OWL 2 RL rule table. The corpus is also a SUBSET: it vendors 262 of the 482 consistency-shaped cases in the upstream manifest, and the harness's OWL2-DL-EXCLUDED line measures the other 220 — 172 of them the tableau decided when probed (108 consistent, 64 inconsistent), so the exclusion was payload-size triage, not a capability limit; 0 do not terminate under a 40 s ceiling (an earlier measurement, before the tableau's clausification and search refinement, found 30; every one of those now resolves within the same ceiling), 25 are withheld (20 reasoner, 5 parse) and 23 carry no RDF/XML premise. Reading 258/262 as coverage of what W3C published overstates it. Every one of those numbers is now GATED rather than free text: scripts/check-doc-claims.py::baseline_note_claim re-derives this note's corpus totals from the generated matrix block in docs/CONFORMANCE.md and its exclusion tally from the frozen census.tsv, and fails make check when they disagree. It is gated because it rotted a whole generation while the ledgered integer beside it stayed correct — this sentence read 261 vendored, 30 non-terminating and 12 withheld against a measured 262, 0 and 25, and nothing in the repository could see it

Entailment (OWL 2 RL, W3C entailment tes.note: W3C's own OWL 2 entailment tests (crates/sparql-conformance/entailment-suite/w3c-owl2-rl/, fetched from https://www.w3.org/2009/11/owl-test/all.rdf), graded through purrdf_entail::entails() — the independent oracle for the rule table, which until it existed was scored only by fixtures authored alongside the rules. 50 cases: all 27 positive entailments W3C places inside the RL profile under RDF-BASED semantics, plus ALL 23 negative entailments (soundness is owed on every case, so nothing is filtered by profile there). The negative lane is 23/23 — no triple W3C publishes as NOT entailed was ever reached, so no unsoundness was found. The positive lane is 27 of 27 and crates/sparql-conformance/src/owl2_rl.rs::LEDGER is EMPTY — 0 schema-conclusion, 0 negative-conclusion, 0 construct-outside-rl, 0 imports-unresolved, 0 ACTIONABLE. Lowered from 1: webont-imports-011's premise owl:imports http://www.w3.org/2002/03owlt/imports/support011-A, and the conclusion is about a class defined only there. The upstream all.rdf export does not carry it inline — an otest:rdfXmlPremiseOntology literal is ONE document — so no reasoner could reach the conclusion from the vendored bytes. The fix was not to reason harder but to VENDOR the missing document: imports/support011-A.rdf, fetched from its own W3C URL on 2026-08-01 with its digest recorded in PROVENANCE.md, kept OUTSIDE cases/ because census_accounts_for_every_upstream_case requires every case directory to have a census row and a support ontology is not a test case. It is keyed by the ontology IRI the document itself declares, not by its file name, and handed to entails() as caller-supplied configuration; the library still fetches nothing, resolution is transitive to a fixpoint, and an unresolved import still refuses by name. Lowered from 4 before that: webont-i5-8-006, -008 and -009 conclude an rdfs:range WIDENED to a containing XSD datatype — WIDENED, not narrowed (xsd:byte is contained in xsd:short), which is why they are sound at all. A property's declared ranges INTERSECT, so -008 needs short & unsignedInt contained in unsignedShort and -009 needs nonNegativeInteger & nonPositiveInteger = {0} contained in short, neither of which is a containment between any two of the datatypes named. Deciding that needs the XSD value spaces, which a rule table has no arithmetic for, so it is decided by the new public purrdf_xsd::range::containment — three-valued, with the NEGATIVE answer gated on the counterexample range being exactly decided, because DataRangeTable::conjunction_is_empty's bool answers `false` for Undecided (right for a clash rule, a silent conversion of undecidable into refuted for a verdict). Lowered from 5 before that: new-feature-reflexiveproperty-001 asserts `knows a owl:ReflexiveProperty` and concludes `Peter knows Peter`. owl:ReflexiveProperty is outside the RL syntax and Profiles §4.3 states no prp-rfl rule — so the PREMISE is outside the syntax too, and a failed match here could never be read as a refutation either. The conclusion is therefore established POSITIVELY, which needs no completeness theorem: OWL 2's RDF-Based Semantics puts <x,x> in EXT(p) for every x in IR when p is reflexive, and every IRI of the conclusion's vocabulary denotes an element of IR. Deliberately NOT closed by an ext-prp-rfl rule: such a clause has no join to constrain its subject, so it would fire once per (term x reflexive property) pair in a lane every consumer runs by default, would put literals in subject position, and would move the calculus contract hash across every committed golden — strict Materialization::OwlRl output is UNCHANGED and extensions(Regime::OwlRl) is still exactly [ext-eq-diff-sym]. Lowered from 7 before that: webont-i5-5-005 concludes an anonymous owl:unionOf class and webont-i5-26-010 an anonymous owl:Restriction. Neither says anything about any individual; each says a CLASS EXISTS, which the RDF-Based semantics' own COMPREHENSION CONDITIONS license — subject to a typing side condition on the operands (unionOf(a) is licensed only for a in IC, and i5-5-005's premise asserting `a rdf:type owl:Class` is exactly why the case is a published entailment rather than a published non-entailment). Only the scaffolds the conclusion names are minted, over blank nodes checked absent from BOTH documents, and membership in a comprehended union is decided by looking for ONE disjunct in the closure — sound trivially, and complete because a consistent Horn theory entails a ground disjunction only by entailing a disjunct. Lowered from 8 before that: chain2trans1 concludes `p rdf:type owl:TransitiveProperty` from `p owl:propertyChainAxiom (p p)`. That axiom abbreviates a universally quantified Horn implication, which is decided by GENERALISATION ON CONSTANTS — freeze `_:a p _:b . _:b p _:c` over constants the premise does not mention, re-run the same table, and prp-spo2 (one of the 78) derives `_:a p _:c`, which is transitivity's own condition; the axiom's other conjunct, p ∈ IOOP, is a lookup in the premise's closure. Deliberately NOT routed through the DL tableau, whose reverse mapping DROPS owl:propertyChainAxiom and would therefore answer a confident wrong False. Lowered from 16 before that: eight cases that conclude a NEGATIVE FACT (an owl:differentFrom, a membership in an anonymous owl:complementOf class) or an owl:AllDifferent collection now AGREE, reached by refutation — assert the conclusion's negation into the premise and re-run the SAME rule table, whose seventeen `false`-concluding rules are the profile's own inconsistency calculus, over a premise whose consistency was established first — and an owl:AllDifferent lowers to the n(n-1)/2 pairwise inequalities OWL 2 defines it as, every one of which must refute. Lowered from 17 before that: webont-differentfrom-001 is reached by a rule declared OUTSIDE every specification table (ext-eq-diff-sym), and every rendered report carries an `extension` line so a caller that must act only on normative conclusions can tell. NONE of these mechanisms adds a rule: rules(Regime::OwlRl) and implemented(Regime::OwlRl) are still exactly the same 78 and extensions(Regime::OwlRl) is still the one ext-eq-diff-sym. Across all five lowerings the rule table did not change once: rules(Regime::OwlRl) and implemented(Regime::OwlRl) are the same 78, extensions(Regime::OwlRl) is the one ext-eq-diff-sym, and strict Materialization::OwlRl output is byte-for-byte what it was. This row, not `OWL-RL 78 / 78`, is the W3C entailment-conformance measurement

GTS transport (frozen vectors).note: 39 frozen cross-language GTS vectors folded through the production reader and compared byte-for-byte with the committed <id>.expected.json each ships; 38 agree exactly. The one ledgered divergence is 12-conflicting-reifier, which binds a single reifier id to two triples and carries no quoted-triple term. rdf:reifies is not a functional property, so both bindings are legitimate and this reader keeps both without complaint - two rows and no diagnostic - while the committed expectation still states the superseded single-binding reading, one row plus a ConflictingReifier diagnostic. The expectation encodes the premise the reader has shed, so correcting it is an upstream act on a corpus governed in gmeow-gts, which this repository never regenerates, edits or deletes. Held to XPASS discipline in both directions: purrdf-gts's frozen_conflicting_reifier_divergence pins both sides in full, and crates/rdf/tests/gts_corpus_expected_fold.rs fails if the listed vector starts AGREEING (the signal to drop the entry and lower this budget to 0) or if any unlisted vector starts disagreeing

rdflib LSP drop-in gate.note: rdflib-suite strict xfails: one SPARQL strictness divergence (an upstream test typo projecting a non-group-key variable), plus four BatchAddGraph tests that name terms with bare relative URIRefs -- rdflib's URIRef is an unvalidated str subclass, while purrdf's IR carries no base and so cannot represent a relative IRI as a term. Both themes are purrdf being STRICTER than rdflib, not purrdf gaps, so these four will not shrink
rdflib LSP drop-in gate.raise_justification: RAISED 1 -> 5 (+4) by the base-IRI work on issue #222. This file's _doc says the budget may only ever be edited DOWNWARD and that a raise must be justified in review, so the justification is recorded here rather than left implicit in the diff. The four added entries are all test_batch_add.py::TestBatchAddGraph (test_exit_submits_partial_batch, test_add_more_than_batch_size, test_add_quad_for_non_conjunctive_pass_on_context_matches, test_no_addN_on_exception). Each names its throwaway terms URIRef('a')/('b%d')/('c%d') -- bare relative references. They were ALREADY semantically broken: a graph holding those terms could never serialize as conformant N-Triples. They passed only because nothing in the old path froze the graph, so the unrepresentable term was never asked to be one. Making a relative IRI a hard error at the IR boundary is what surfaced them. The four are a permanent divergence, not a gap: rdflib's URIRef is an unvalidated str subclass and purrdf's cannot be under .goals, which forbids minting or inventing a base. Closing the gap would require inventing a base (forbidden -- it would differ per machine and leak local paths into published RDF) or admitting terms with no knowable identity into the IR. What the tests actually exercise -- BatchAddGraph's batching -- purrdf implements correctly; only their choice of term spelling is unusable here. This budget must therefore NOT be lowered by weakening purrdf's validation. NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW SIGN-OFF: this is the one upward edit in this change set.

Python binding suite.note: purrdf.compat differential strict xfails vs rdflib 7.6 (the suite's only ledgered entries)
